_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see. The shape changed with it — safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. limits is ONE string, server-written, never the model’s. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation; it uses driver_state "fine" deliberately, because on a tired run factors_in_favor is often legitimately empty and pinning it non-empty made this check flap. Case 5 is the grounding case: this exact input produced "Heavy traffic — evening commute conditions", "low-visibility weather", a 20-30 minute recovery prescription and safer_options inventing a colleague and someone at home. Structure alone will not catch a regression there — READ case 5 after any prompt change. router.outputGuard is live, so expect "v2 guard: FAIL (n field(s))" on the pause cases; that is the guard working. supplied_fact_upgraded / invented_person_or_circumstance / invented_recovery_interval are the three terms added for case 5.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you've reported gives a clear reason to wait — proceeding appears reasonable.
output.summary: You report feeling fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is short. Staying later than planned is worth noting, but on its own it doesn't change the picture you've described.
output.main_concern: Late-night driving on city streets can involve less predictable road users — worth staying attentive.
factors_harder: Late night — you are aware of this, and it affects what you need to watch for
City streets — intersections, pedestrians, cyclists, and varying signal timing
factors_in_favor: You are aware of the late hour
output.before_you_decide: If 'fine' is masking more tiredness than you're giving it credit for — heavy eyes, slower reactions, difficulty focusing — that changes the call. Do a honest check before you start the car.
prep_checklist: Sit in the car for a moment and honestly reassess how alert you feel before moving
Adjust mirrors and seat before departure
Keep phone out of reach or on silent — interact with it only when parked
Note your fuel level before pulling away
Drive to the conditions: city streets at night may have pedestrians or cyclists less visible than in daylight
watch_for: Eyes feeling heavy or difficulty keeping them fully open
Drifting within your lane or toward lane markings
Slower-than-usual reaction to lights or intersections
Any feeling that you are not fully tracking what is happening around you
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Hold off until you know what the pass conditions are — that one fact changes this call.
output.summary: You have reported snow or ice and high wind on a highway drive, and you have not driven in winter conditions for several months. The unknown state of the pass is a concrete gap that should be filled before you leave.
output.main_concern: You do not know current pass conditions, and that uncertainty — combined with reported snow or ice, high wind, and limited recent winter-driving experience — is reason enough to wait before starting.
factors_harder: Reported snow or ice on route
No winter driving since last winter — reduced recent practice
output.before_you_decide: Before you leave, check what the current conditions are on the route between Denver and Cheyenne — specifically the pass area where you feel uncertain. If an official source shows closure, traction requirements you cannot meet, or conditions that do not match what you are comfortable with, that is reason to wait. If conditions are reported as passable and your hesitation eases, reassess then.
safer_options: Check the official state road-conditions line or CDOT / WYDOT site for current pass status before leaving
Wait and reassess once conditions or your comfort level have changed
Ask a rested, winter-experienced driver to take the wheel, if one is available
Consider whether the trip can be delayed to a time with better-reported conditions
Confirm your vehicle is fit for the conditions you reported — working defroster, good visibility, adequate tread — before leaving.
watch_for: Any official closure or traction-law restriction posted for the pass
Worsening wind or visibility once underway — consider pulling off if control feels uncertain
Fatigue or increased anxiety building during the drive
Reduced traction when braking or accelerating
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurz pausieren und die Umleitung klären, bevor Sie starten.
output.summary: Sie fühlen sich gut, aber zwei konkrete Unsicherheiten sprechen für einen kurzen Aufschub: Regen und Nebel als aktuelle Bedingungen und eine Ihnen unbekannte Umleitungsstrecke durch die Baustelle. Bei 75 Minuten Fahrtzeit auf gemischten Straßen mit starkem Verkehr und spätnächtlicher Stunde lohnt es sich, diese Punkte zu klären, bevor Sie losfahren.
output.main_concern: Sie kennen die Umleitungsstrecke durch die Baustelle nicht — das bedeutet zusätzliche Aufmerksamkeit für Abbiegungen und Beschilderung, besonders wenn Regen und Nebel die Sicht einschränken.
factors_harder: Gemischte Straßen — verschiedene Straßentypen erfordern Aufmerksamkeitswechsel
factors_in_favor: Fahrer fühlt sich nach eigener Aussage gut
output.before_you_decide: Verschaffen Sie sich vor der Abfahrt einen groben Überblick über die Umleitungsstrecke, damit Sie die wesentlichen Abbiegungen kennen — und beurteilen Sie dann, ob die Sicht gut genug ist, dass Sie sich sicher fühlen, jetzt loszufahren.
safer_options: Umleitungsstrecke anhand einer Karte oder Beschilderungsinformation vorab grob einprägen, dann neu entscheiden
Warten, bis sich die Sichtbedingungen verbessern — erst aufbrechen, wenn Sie sich damit wohl fühlen
Starker Verkehr bei Nacht und Regen — erhöhte Aufmerksamkeit nötig
Öffentliche Verkehrsmittel prüfen, falls noch welche fahren
An einem sicheren Ort warten und die Lage neu einschätzen, bevor Sie starten
watch_for: Sicht verschlechtert sich weiter, sodass Sie Fahrbahnmarkierungen oder vorausfahrende Fahrzeuge kaum noch erkennen können
Sie die Umleitungsstrecke nicht kennen und plötzlich nicht mehr wissen, wohin Sie fahren sollen
Unerwartete Hindernisse oder Absperrungen im Baustellenbereich
Fahrtrichtung oder Abbiegungen aufgrund schlechter Sicht oder unerwarteter Beschilderung verfehlen
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

input.concern: I caught myself yawning on the walk to the car and it is raining harder than when I arrived.

output.headline: Worth pausing briefly before committing to this drive.
output.summary: You reported feeling a little tired, caught yourself yawning, and the rain has picked up since you arrived. Combined with heavy traffic and a 45-minute mixed-road drive in the evening, a brief pause to reassess makes sense.
output.main_concern: You reported feeling a little tired and caught yourself yawning before leaving the office. The rain has also picked up since you arrived. You are facing 45 minutes on mixed roads in evening heavy traffic. Those conditions together warrant a pause to check in w
factors_harder: Caught yawning before even starting the drive
Rain is heavier now than when you arrived
45 minutes on mixed roads in the evening
output.before_you_decide: If, after waiting somewhere safe and off the road, you feel clearly alert and are comfortable with the rain and traffic conditions, that is the point to reassess whether to go.
safer_options: Wait somewhere safe — inside if possible — and reassess before leaving; go only if you feel clearly alert
Step outside or find a quiet spot for a few minutes if you can, and notice whether you feel more alert. That clarity is what matters for the reassessment.
Ask a rested person to drive, if someone is available
Check whether staying longer at your current location until conditions or your alertness improve is an option
watch_for: Eyes feeling heavy or slow to refocus while driving
Drifting within your lane or catching yourself correcting
Missing a traffic signal, sign, or gap in traffic you would normally catch
Rain intensity making it hard to see clearly
Reaction time feeling slower than usual in stop-and-go traffic
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.
